report.incidentSummary: On 2026-09-30 starting at 11:07 IST (05:37 UTC), KYC submissions began failing for users attempting onboarding. While the initial incident report dismissed the kyc-service deployment because it was recorded at 16:35 IST in UTC-indexed logs, investigation revealed that deployment CHG-48220 (v1.15.3 to v1.16.0) executed at 11:05 IST (05:35 UTC) from Mumbai Jenkins (legacy-jenkins-mum). Immediately following the deployment, kyc-service error rates spiked from ~0.4% to ~9.4% due to internal HTTP 500 serialization errors rejecting the new residency_type enum value 'NRI_OCI'.
report.rootCauseStatement: Deployment CHG-48220 of kyc-service v1.16.0 introduced a serialization error where the enum value 'NRI_OCI' for field residency_type is unhandled or unrecognized during submission processing, triggering internal HTTP 500 errors on KYC submission requests.

hypotheses.cause: Deployment CHG-48220 (v1.15.3 to v1.16.0) introduced an unhandled or mismatched enum serialization bug for residency_type 'NRI_OCI', causing internal HTTP 500 errors on KYC submission requests.
hypotheses.rationale: kyc-service error rates jumped from ~0.4% to ~9.4% right after the 05:35 UTC deployment of v1.16.0. Logs explicitly verify HTTP 500 errors on version 1.16.0 with message: 'serialization error: unknown enum value \'NRI_OCI\' for field residency_type'.

hypotheses.cause: External partner kyc-agency API contract divergence or upstream degradation rejecting or failing requests.
hypotheses.rationale: Agency p95 latency remained steady at ~1779 ms without spikes or timeouts, and the failure occurs internally within kyc-service v1.16.0 prior to or during serialization rather than via partner API rejection or network timeouts.

facts.statement: kyc-service error_rate rose from baseline ~0.34%-0.45% to 2.16% at 05:35 UTC, and stabilized at ~9.35%-9.47% from 05:40 UTC through 11:45 UTC.

Starting at 2026-09-30T05:37:00.962Z, kyc-service logged 794 occurrences of ERROR with HTTP status 500: 'KYC <ref> submit failed: serialization error: unknown enum value \'NRI_OCI\' for field residency_type' on version 1.16.0.
Agency p95 latency (mean 1779 ms) and service p95 latency (mean 686.5 ms) remained steady with no spikes or timeouts around 05:37 UTC.
api-gateway error rates on /v1/kyc stayed flat at ~0.35%, and database connections, slow queries, and lock wait times remained normal throughout the window.

kyc-service deployment CHG-48220 (v1.15.3 -> v1.16.0, 'release: NRI/OCI residency types in KYC submission') was recorded at 2026-09-30T11:05:00.000 without timezone (tz: 'none') on legacy-jenkins-mum.

inferences.statement: Deployer legacy-jenkins-mum is in Mumbai (IST, UTC+05:30), meaning the recorded 11:05:00 timestamp represents 11:05 IST (05:35 UTC), exactly 2 minutes prior to the first error at 05:37 UTC. The SRE was misled by the change store indexing local time as UTC (11:05 UTC = 16:35 IST).

The KYC submission failures are driven strictly by internal enum serialization exceptions on residency_type 'NRI_OCI' introduced in v1.16.0 rather than database contention or third-party agency degradation.

assumptions.statement: legacy-jenkins-mum emits build timestamps in local IST without explicit timezone offset formatting.

timeline.event: Deployment CHG-48220 executes on legacy-jenkins-mum, rolling out kyc-service v1.16.0 with NRI/OCI residency types support.
kyc-service error rate ticks up to 2.16%.
First HTTP 500 error logged on kyc-service v1.16.0: 'serialization error: unknown enum value \'NRI_OCI\' for field residency_type'.
kyc-service error rate reaches ~9.37%, persisting above 9.3% across the incident window.
Incident INC-5216 reported by On-call SRE suspecting kyc-agency due to release timestamp confusion.

confidence.rationale: High confidence supported by exact matching log messages specifying version 1.16.0, the specific failing enum value 'NRI_OCI', and tight temporal alignment with deployment CHG-48220 once timezone offset is accounted for.

gaps.description: Source code diff of build-59012 showing the exact enum definition and serialization mapping was not directly inspected due to tool call budget limits.
gaps.impact: Minimal impact; the runtime log message explicitly identifies the unknown enum value and field name.

recommendedActions.action: Roll back kyc-service to version 1.15.3 immediately or deploy a hotfix that includes 'NRI_OCI' in the residency_type enum serializer.
recommendedActions.rationale: Restores KYC onboarding functionality by eliminating the serialization exception.
recommendedActions.verification: Check kyc-service error_rate returns to baseline (~0.4%) and no further 'serialization error' logs appear.

recommendedActions.action: Configure legacy-jenkins-mum to emit ISO 8601 timestamps with explicit UTC timezone offsets (+05:30 or Z).
recommendedActions.rationale: Prevents change ingestion systems from mistaking IST local timestamps for UTC, avoiding misleading incident triage delays.
recommendedActions.verification: Inspect future build and deploy event payloads from legacy-jenkins-mum in the change tracking service to ensure timezone metadata is present.

recommendedActions.action: Add unit and integration tests covering enum serialization and deserialization for all supported residency types in kyc-service CI pipelines.
recommendedActions.rationale: Prevents future regressions where schema additions are not properly mapped in serialization libraries.
recommendedActions.verification: Verify CI pipeline build fails when an unregistered or unmapped enum variant is passed to the submission serializer.

incident.title: KYC submissions failing
incident.summary: KYC submissions failing for some users since about 11:07 IST. The kyc-service release is logged at 16:35 IST, hours after the failures started, so it's not the release. The KYC agency has been slow today.
symptoms: KYC submissions fail for some users

candidates.cause: Upstream latency or failure in kyc-agency causing outbound submission timeouts exceeding kyc-service or api-gateway thresholds
candidates.whyPlausible: kyc-service calls kyc-agency synchronously with a 5000ms timeout while api-gateway enforces a 3000ms timeout on kyc-service. If kyc-agency latency spikes as noted by the reporter, requests will time out and fail for users.

candidates.wouldRuleOut: kyc-service metrics show agency_latency_p95_ms remained normal (<2000ms) with zero agency timeouts or HTTP 5xx errors from kyc-agency during the incident window.

candidates.cause: External rate limiting or quota exhaustion imposed by kyc-agency on KYC submission API calls
candidates.whyPlausible: Submissions are failing for some users rather than all, which is typical of throttle thresholds or per-minute rate limits being hit at the third-party agency during business hours.
candidates.wouldConfirm: kyc-service logs reveal HTTP 429 Too Many Requests responses or explicit rate limit error payloads from kyc-agency endpoints starting at ~05:37 UTC.
candidates.wouldRuleOut: kyc-service logs show no HTTP 429 responses from kyc-agency, or error codes are internal 5xx / database errors rather than throttling responses.

# Investigation report: KYC submissions failing

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** critic_accepted · **Confidence:** 0.95 · **Written by:** reporting agent

## Summary
On 2026-09-30 starting at 11:07 IST (05:37 UTC), KYC submissions began failing for users attempting onboarding. While the initial incident report dismissed the kyc-service deployment because it was recorded at 16:35 IST in UTC-indexed logs, investigation revealed that deployment CHG-48220 (v1.15.3 to v1.16.0) executed at 11:05 IST (05:35 UTC) from Mumbai Jenkins (legacy-jenkins-mum). Immediately following the deployment, kyc-service error rates spiked from ~0.4% to ~9.4% due to internal HTTP 500 serialization errors rejecting the new residency_type enum value 'NRI_OCI'.

**Root cause:** Deployment CHG-48220 of kyc-service v1.16.0 introduced a serialization error where the enum value 'NRI_OCI' for field residency_type is unhandled or unrecognized during submission processing, triggering internal HTTP 500 errors on KYC submission requests.

## Hypotheses
1. **Deployment CHG-48220 (v1.15.3 to v1.16.0) introduced an unhandled or mismatched enum serialization bug for residency_type 'NRI_OCI', causing internal HTTP 500 errors on KYC submission requests.** — `kyc-service`, deployment_regression, confidence 0.95, supported
   - Supporting: [ev_1, ev_4, ev_7, ev_8, ev_13, ev_14] · Contradicting: none
   - kyc-service error rates jumped from ~0.4% to ~9.4% right after the 05:35 UTC deployment of v1.16.0. Logs explicitly verify HTTP 500 errors on version 1.16.0 with message: 'serialization error: unknown enum value \'NRI_OCI\' for field residency_type'.
2. **External partner kyc-agency API contract divergence or upstream degradation rejecting or failing requests.** — `kyc-agency`, upstream_dependency_degradation, confidence 0.05, ruled_out
   - Supporting: [ev_1, ev_8] · Contradicting: [ev_2, ev_3, ev_13]
   - Agency p95 latency remained steady at ~1779 ms without spikes or timeouts, and the failure occurs internally within kyc-service v1.16.0 prior to or during serialization rather than via partner API rejection or network timeouts.

## Facts
- kyc-service error_rate rose from baseline ~0.34%-0.45% to 2.16% at 05:35 UTC, and stabilized at ~9.35%-9.47% from 05:40 UTC through 11:45 UTC. [ev_4]
- Starting at 2026-09-30T05:37:00.962Z, kyc-service logged 794 occurrences of ERROR with HTTP status 500: 'KYC <ref> submit failed: serialization error: unknown enum value \'NRI_OCI\' for field residency_type' on version 1.16.0. [ev_1, ev_7, ev_8]
- Agency p95 latency (mean 1779 ms) and service p95 latency (mean 686.5 ms) remained steady with no spikes or timeouts around 05:37 UTC. [ev_2, ev_3]
- api-gateway error rates on /v1/kyc stayed flat at ~0.35%, and database connections, slow queries, and lock wait times remained normal throughout the window. [ev_5, ev_6, ev_9, ev_10, ev_11, ev_15]
- kyc-service deployment CHG-48220 (v1.15.3 -> v1.16.0, 'release: NRI/OCI residency types in KYC submission') was recorded at 2026-09-30T11:05:00.000 without timezone (tz: 'none') on legacy-jenkins-mum. [ev_13, ev_14]

## Inferences
- Deployer legacy-jenkins-mum is in Mumbai (IST, UTC+05:30), meaning the recorded 11:05:00 timestamp represents 11:05 IST (05:35 UTC), exactly 2 minutes prior to the first error at 05:37 UTC. The SRE was misled by the change store indexing local time as UTC (11:05 UTC = 16:35 IST). [ev_13, ev_14]
- The KYC submission failures are driven strictly by internal enum serialization exceptions on residency_type 'NRI_OCI' introduced in v1.16.0 rather than database contention or third-party agency degradation. [ev_1, ev_2, ev_3, ev_8]

## Assumptions
- legacy-jenkins-mum emits build timestamps in local IST without explicit timezone offset formatting.

## Timeline
- **2026-09-30 11:05 IST (05:35:00 UTC)** Deployment CHG-48220 executes on legacy-jenkins-mum, rolling out kyc-service v1.16.0 with NRI/OCI residency types support. [ev_13, ev_14]
- **2026-09-30 11:05 IST (05:35:00 UTC)** kyc-service error rate ticks up to 2.16%. [ev_4]
- **2026-09-30 11:07 IST (05:37:00 UTC)** First HTTP 500 error logged on kyc-service v1.16.0: 'serialization error: unknown enum value \'NRI_OCI\' for field residency_type'. [ev_1, ev_8]
- **2026-09-30 11:10 IST (05:40:00 UTC)** kyc-service error rate reaches ~9.37%, persisting above 9.3% across the incident window. [ev_4]
